# Testing LLMs as a Swimming Tutor

### In this task, I explored how the use of *structured prompting* can shape the behavior of an LLM. To do so, I tried to emulate a tutoring session with the LLM (Anthropic/Claude-3.5-sonnet) both without and with a detailed prompt. For the first session, I just asked the LLM to be my tutor and teach me how to swim without any further prompting. For the second session, I used Ethan Mollick's structured tutor prompt before asking the LLM to teach me how to swim. I continued both for ~15 minutes and in the first half, I tried to remain on topic. For the second half, I attempted to derail the LLM by going off topic and asking irrelevant questions. I also did a third task where I tried to revise the Mollick prompt and improve it. 

+ Task1.ipynb contains the entire interaction for the first session (without a structured prompt)
+ Task2.ipynb contains the entire interaction for the second session (with the Mollick prompt). Also contains my reflection after both interactions.
+ Task3.ipynb contains the entire interaction for the third session (slightly modified Mollick prompt) and a reflection.
